title: Split long-lived Terraform anchors and add provider compatibility shim for cloud-provider upgrades
creator: Maya Singh
description: Background: Our monolithic Terraform anchors (vpc_root, shared_networking, egress_blueprint) have grown large over time and cause slow plan/apply cycles, interdependent provider pinning, and risky changes during routine updates. The AWS provider v5 upgrade introduced breaking semantics for certain resource attribute names and default behaviors; those changes currently block a number of downstream workstreams. Goal: Decompose long-lived anchors into smaller, well-scoped modules (core-network, transit-gateways, nat-lifecycle, egress-ipam), standardize module outputs, and introduce a lightweight provider-compatibility shim that allows workspaces to transition from aws provider v4 to v5 incrementally. Scope: - Split existing anchor modules and produce compatibility wrappers - Add automated integration tests in CI to validate both provider versions against a small staging workspace - Provide a migration path for regional workspaces with a canary rollout and zero-downtime route cutover - Update documentation and runbook for operators
acceptance_criteria: Monorepo anchor modules split into at least four smaller modules with preserved public API (inputs/outputs)
Compatibility shim module present and documented; same Terraform code can be applied with either provider v4 or v5 by toggling provider alias flag
End-to-end CI job validates module applies and plan/diff for both provider versions and fails on drift
A canary workspace in eu-west-1 has migrated using this process with no customer-facing incidents
Module outputs follow the new naming convention and a migration script exists to convert downstream consumers
migration_plan: 1) Discovery: run terraform graph and usage scan for all inputs/outputs that reference anchor modules
2) Prototype: author core-network and nat-lifecycle modules in a feature branch; add provider-compat shim with alias provider pattern
3) CI: add integration job that spins up minimal test infra in sandbox and validates both provider versions
4) Split: land module splits behind feature flags and publish new module versions to internal registry
5) Canary: migrate 1 non-critical regional workspace (eu-west-1) during a low-traffic window using transient resources and route cutover
6) Rollout: migrate remaining workspaces in waves, monitor metrics, and update downstream stacks to new module outputs
7) Deprecate: once all workspaces are migrated, remove shim and mark old anchors deprecated
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Output renaming will break downstream stacks. Mitigation: provide a migration script and keep old outputs available via compatibility alias for 2 cycles

Risk: Provider v5 behavioral changes could change resource replacement behavior (e.g., subnet tagging defaults). Mitigation: run staged applies in sandbox and compare resource IDs, add provider-specific acceptance tests
Risk: Long apply windows during migration causing API throttling. Mitigation: rate-limit applies, use smaller parallelism, and schedule low-traffic windows
Risk: Unknown edge-case in on-prem Private deployments. Mitigation: coordinate with Private infra team and perform an isolated dry-run in the Private staging environment
testing_and_validation: Add a new CI matrix job terraform-compat that runs terraform init/plan/apply/destroy with provider v4 and v5 against minimal fixtures
Unit tests for module input validation (terratest where applicable)
Pre- and post-migration smoke checks against Redwood Console: route availability, LB health, and NAT gateway metrics
Post-apply reconciliation job that runs terraform plan and alerts on unexpected diffs for 24h after migration
rollback_plan: If canary migration causes regressions, run rollback by re-applying previous module versions from registry and toggling provider alias back to v4
Maintain snapshot of state files before each wave and use state rollback for urgent revert
If traffic impact observed, cut traffic back to previous region using global routing rules and abort further waves
